$comment: Allowlist of PERMISSIBLE first-party / open price sources for the scheduled refresh (scripts/refresh_prices.mjs). GOVERNANCE HARD RULE: only pub/brewery OFFICIAL sites and open-data feeds may appear here. NEVER add a competitor price-aggregator or any site whose terms forbid automated access. Every source must be a first-party publisher of its own prices, or an open-licensed dataset. The refresh script reads this file and (in a real run) fetches ONLY these URLs; it will refuse any URL not listed here.

sources.label: Example Brewery — official taproom page
sources.note: PLACEHOLDER. Replace with a real brewery/pub official menu page you have permission to read. First-party publisher of their own pint prices.

sources.label: Example open-data pub dataset

$drinkSourcesComment: Allowlist of PERMISSIBLE first-party / open DRINK-menu price sources for scripts/refresh_drink_prices.mjs (E2 of docs/PRD_ALL_DRINKS.md). Same hard rule as `sources` above: a chain publishing ITS OWN pub menus (e.g. Wetherspoons' own site/app for its own pubs) is first-party and permissible. Competitor price aggregators, review sites (Vivino, Untappd, etc.) or any site whose ToS/robots.txt forbids automated access are NEVER permissible, no exceptions. `kind` must be one of first-party-chain | first-party-venue | open-data. Every entry must be `permissible: true` AND documented with a `licence` string; the refresh script refuses any source that is missing either.

drinkSources.label: J D Wetherspoon — official site (per-pub menus)
drinkSources.licence: All rights reserved — first-party publisher of its own pub menus/prices; read-only, attributed use only. No republishing of the source's own copy, only the price fact + observedAt + link back.
drinkSources.notes: STUB ONLY — see scripts/refresh_drink_prices.mjs fetchFromDrinkSource(). Wetherspoons publishes a per-pub menu (food + drinks with prices) on jdwetherspoon.com, and this chain is the flagship first-party permissible source named in the PRD. Before any real fetch/parse ships: (1) fetch and read https://www.jdwetherspoon.com/robots.txt and confirm the specific per-pub menu paths are not disallowed; (2) read the site's Terms of Use for any automated-access restriction and honour it (rate-limit, identify a contact UA, no login-walled pages); (3) pick a STABLE parse target — a single per-pub menu URL pattern whose markup/JSON is unlikely to change release-to-release — and pin a fixture/snapshot test to detect silent breakage; (4) never scrape at a rate that could be mistaken for abuse (cache aggressively, refresh at most daily, back off on non-200s); (5) stamp every row with this source's licence + url + an accurate observedAt, and drop (do not guess) any row that can't be attributed to a specific pub.
